behavioral_effects: The wishlist-calls-fail-gracefully exception is recorded and wired: /api/auth/password/change (settings/account) and /api/health/ready (admin/system) no longer count as broken chains
An exception excuses a single call, not a page: one classified wishlist call cannot silence an unclassified break on the same page
compatibility_impact: The no-broken-site-chains check now consumes accepted exceptions per call, matching the convention its sibling checks already use; existing exceptions are unaffected because none carried a matching scope string before
follow_up: Classify or fix the /api/users/{param} call on settings/account: either wire the delete-account endpoint through the proxy or record its own reviewed exception
Retire the exception when the backend lands a password-change endpoint or a per-service /health/ready
limitations: The /settings/account page also calls DELETE /api/users/{id} (account self-deletion), which nothing serves and which was not in the sweep's verified classification - it remains counted as a broken chain, deliberately unexcepted
reason: The settings/account page calls /api/auth/password/change and the admin/system page calls /api/health/ready; both endpoints do not exist yet, both pages handle the failure gracefully by design, and both calls are documented wishlist surface - without a scoped accepted exception the no-broken-site-chains rule counts them as defects on every sweep, burying real breaks
rollback: Revert the commit: the exception entry, the rule's exception_ref, the check wiring, and the test all disappear together and the two wishlist calls are counted again
security_impact: None - the exception excuses two calls that already failed gracefully; no endpoint, auth, or data path changed. The check change cannot widen an exception's reach: scope strings name one page-file plus one path each
summary: Record accepted exceptions for the two documented wishlist calls so no-broken-site-chains stops counting them
